A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mocap-2-to-3, and all supplied text, figures, tables, and equations are readable. However, both end with references: v4's cited Appendices B.2/B.3 and v6's referenced supplementary material are absent. This limits comparison of detailed camera configurations and implementation procedures.

before.justification: v4 reports original RICH and AIST++ evaluations, qualitative reconstructions, and component ablations in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–7.

after.justification: v6 retains these original evaluations and ablations in Tables 2–4 and Figures 5–7, with additional baseline results.

M1.justification: The documented pipeline retains single-view diffusion pretraining, four-view fine-tuning, view attention, local/global decomposition, pointmap conditioning, and triangulation. Section 3.5 clarifies that existing SMPLify fitting is optional when mesh parameters are required; it does not establish a different lifting algorithm.

E1.justification: Both use HumanML3D, BEDLAM, and Human3.6M for training and evaluate ground-truth SMPL keypoint lifting on RICH and ViTPose-derived COCO keypoint lifting on AIST++. The added COCO teaser panel does not introduce a new task or dataset.

E2.justification: v6 adds TRAM to the RICH comparison and GVHMR+SMPLify to the AIST++ comparison, while retaining the other evaluated comparators. MetricHMR appears in the new related-method feature table, without reported benchmark evaluation.

E3.justification: Metrics, detector inputs, and reported ablation budgets remain unchanged. However, v4 Section 3.2 specifies test-set camera perspectives during testing, whereas v6 specifies random sampling of pretraining camera poses during fine-tuning and omits the testing rule. These concern different stages; the missing camera-configuration supplements prevent establishing whether the test-time protocol changed.

E4.justification: v6 removes the AIST++ control without AIST++ 2D pretraining and its associated robustness argument from v4 Table 2 and Section 4.3. The RICH ablations testing motion decomposition, pointmaps, convergence, and in-domain pretraining remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Added result rows retain the same single-value reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are identical. v6 adds TRAM's RICH results, including 36.3 PA-MPJPE and 533.8 Abs-MPJPE, and AIST++ GVHMR+SMPLify results of 62.2/102.8/112.3 for PA-MPJPE/MPJPE/Troot. It removes the no-AIST++-pretraining results of 61.2/92.4/64.7. It also removes v4's inconsistent 111.5-mm Abs-MPJPE statement; both RICH tables report 156.8 mm.

T1.justification: The coordinate decomposition, global-recovery Equation (1), and pointmap geometry remain mathematically equivalent. Notation changes and expanded explanations do not introduce a new derivation, theorem, or proof in the supplied material.

C1.justification: v6 drops v4's explicit characterization of absolute monocular pose recovery as a novel task. The principal claims about 2D pretraining, absolute positioning, generalization, and comparative performance remain. Listing ground encoding as a separate contribution restates an existing component.

C2.justification: v6 adds rationale for diffusion over deterministic regression and calibrated cameras over potentially drifting SLAM estimates. It reframes inaccurate detector inputs as an upstream issue rather than an intrinsic framework limitation, and replaces planned SLAM-based camera estimation with future interaction applications. The ground-plane coordinate requirement is also more explicit.

D1.justification: v6 newly specifies 175 in-domain RICH sequences, identifies the RICH training set as a pretraining source, and clarifies baseline input requirements. These disclosures do not establish changed sample counts or inputs. A project-page link replaces v4's future-code promise, but the PDFs do not establish whether code is available.

R1.justification: v6 adds MetricHMR, removes the ZoeDepth citation, introduces a related-method feature comparison, and sharpens the distinction between calibrated-camera and SLAM-based absolute recovery. The central positioning around 2D pretraining and absolute localization remains. Updated MVLift and SLAHMR bibliographic entries represent retained methods.

P1.justification: v6 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations. It creates numbered related-work subsections, renames method subsections, separates limitations from the conclusion, and changes author, affiliation, acknowledgment, and citation formatting.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a redesigned full-width teaser preceding the abstract, with an added COCO-results panel. v6 adds the method-feature comparison table, revises diagram labels and quantitative-table legends, and substantially changes the opening layout and document formatting. Figures 5–7 retain their underlying qualitative comparisons.

improvement.justification: The added baseline comparisons and clearer input/data disclosures improve transparency, while removing the 111.5-mm prose error resolves a contradiction with the RICH table. Deleting the AIST++ pretraining control weakens one generalization argument, but the retained RICH ablations preserve relevant evidence. The net improvement is limited; core results are unchanged and referenced supplementary details remain unavailable.
